<!-- Default submission instructions. They follow the config: the repository method
     when submissions$repos$registry is set, the bucket unless
     submissions$use_bucket is false. Override with the challenge's own
     _content/instructions-submit.qmd, e.g. to describe a helper function. -->

```{r}
#| include: false
use_github <- !is.null(cfg$submissions$repos$registry)
use_bucket <- !isFALSE(cfg$submissions$use_bucket)
example_theme <- themes[1]
fence <- strrep("`", 3)
register_step <- if (isTRUE(cfg$submissions$repos$issue_registration)) {
  paste0("[Register your repository](https://github.com/", cfg$github_repo,
         "/issues/new?template=register-forecast-repo.yml) by opening an issue, giving its address ",
         "and saying where your forecasts go. A bot checks it and replies on the issue.")
} else {
  paste0("Ask us to add your repository to the list we read: email ", settings$contact_email,
         " with its address and whether your forecasts go to the repository or the submissions bucket.")
}
example_link <- if (!is.null(settings$example_submission_repo)) {
  paste0("\nSee a complete, working example at [", settings$example_submission_repo,
         "](https://github.com/", settings$example_submission_repo, ").\n")
} else {
  ""
}
results_url <- challengeci::bucket_uri(cfg, "forecasts_bucket", "submission_results",
                                       "<model_id>.csv", scheme = "https")
```

```{r}
#| output: asis
#| echo: false
if (use_github) {
  cat(if (use_bucket) '#### From a git repository\n' else '',
      '
Every model has a **public** repository, on GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Codeberg or Hugging Face, that describes it. Nothing needs to be uploaded: we read new forecast files from the repository.

1)  Add a file named `challenge-model.yaml` at the top of the repository that says which models it submits for this challenge, and describes them (the questions of the [registration form](', settings$registration_form_url, ') are the other keys, answered the same way; leave out any you do not want to answer):

', fence, 'yaml
challenge: ', cfg$project_id, '
models:
  - model_id: my_model
    path: forecasts/
    long_name: My model
    description: How my model works
    model_type: process-based
', fence, '

2)  Commit each forecast to the `forecasts/` folder as a `.csv` or `.csv.gz` file. **The file name does not matter**: we read the `model_id` and `reference_datetime` columns in the file, so one file can hold several variables, and the same file can go to every challenge that lists your model. Each challenge keeps only the rows that belong to it, those with its variables, durations and sites, and tells you how many it dropped.
3)  ', register_step, '

A forecast needs the columns `model_id`, `reference_datetime`, `datetime`, `site_id`, `variable`, `duration`, `family`, `parameter` and `prediction`. An optional `project_id` column labels the challenge a row is for; leave it out for rows meant for every challenge that lists your model. If a forecast for the same model, reference date, variable and duration is already stored, the first one is kept and the repeated rows are dropped. A file is read the first time we see it, and later edits to it are ignored. We check each new file and publish the result, including the reason when a file is rejected, at `', results_url, '`.
', example_link, sep = '')
}
if (use_bucket) {
  cat(if (use_github) '\n#### Upload to the submissions bucket\n\n' else '',
      if (use_github) paste0('If your registration says your forecasts go to the bucket, name each file `<theme>-<YYYY-MM-DD>-<model_id>.csv.gz`, for example `', example_theme, '-2026-01-01-my_model.csv.gz`, and upload it.\n\n') else '',
      'Upload the file to the `', cfg$submissions_bucket, '` bucket at `https://',
      cfg$submissions_endpoint, '` with any S3 client. If you need upload access, email ',
      settings$contact_email, '.\n', sep = '')
}
```
